name: Free Image CDN
author: Chema

sections.description:
Speed up your images with a free CDN, without configuration. The plugin rewrites the images of your site so they are delivered from wsrv.nl, a free and open source image CDN built on nginx, libvips and Cloudflare.

Once activated, every image stored in /wp-content/ that appears on a page (the src and srcset attributes of your image tags and the url() of your CSS) is served from https://wsrv.nl/?url=https://your-site.com/wp-content/.... Your server keeps the original files; wsrv.nl caches a copy and serves it from the data center closest to each visitor.

Why it helps

  • Your server sends fewer bytes, so it can handle more visitors with the same hosting.
  • Images are cached worldwide and served with a one year expiration, so repeat visits do not touch your server at all.
  • No settings to configure and no files to move: activate the plugin and it works.

Key Features

  • Crazy Fast: Performance is not just an afterthought; it’s a core feature. Enjoy lightning-fast loading times for your images.
  • Awesome Technology: We employ best-in-class technologies such as nginx and libvips to ensure top-notch image processing.
  • Free / Open Source: wsrv.nl is an open-source project, so you can save your money for other essential tasks.
  • Worldwide Cache: Benefit from a global cache that manipulates images on-the-fly, ensuring optimal performance.
  • CDN Caching: Leverage Cloudflare’s global network of 200+ data centers to cache and deliver your images for the fastest load times.
  • Widely Used: Join the community of users who process 6 million images per hour, generating around 400TB of outbound traffic each month.
  • Simple Install: Easily integrate the CDN service into your WordPress website for quick and hassle-free image processing.

Good to know

  • The plugin has no settings screen. Activate it and that’s it.
  • It switches itself off on local sites (localhost, 127.0.0.1, .local, .localhost, .test, .docksal, .dev.cc, .lndo.site and any site whose environment type is local), so it never interferes with your development.
  • The HTML is rewritten with output buffering, so images added by page builders, shortcodes or other plugins are covered too.
  • Only images hosted in your own /wp-content/ directory are rewritten. Images that already come from another CDN are left alone.
  • SVG files are skipped on purpose: wsrv.nl converts them to PNG, which would ruin vector logos and icons.

License

This plugin is released under the GPLv2 or later license. See http://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-2.0.html

Acknowledgments

We want to express our gratitude to wsrv.nl for providing a free and efficient image CDN service that benefits the WordPress community.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the Plugins > Add New screen, or upload the free-image-cdn folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. That’s it. Open your site and check that your image addresses now start with https://wsrv.nl/?url=.
sections.faq:
Do I need an account or an API key?

No. wsrv.nl is a free and open source service and the plugin only builds the image addresses. There is nothing to sign up for and nothing to configure.

What is a CDN (Content Delivery Network)?

A CDN is a network of servers distributed across various locations globally, designed to deliver web content, including images, more efficiently to users. By using a CDN, you can reduce the load on your web hosting server and improve the speed and reliability of content delivery.

Why should I use a CDN for images?

Using a CDN for images offers several advantages, including faster loading times, reduced server load, improved performance, and a better user experience. CDNs store cached copies of your images on multiple servers worldwide, ensuring that users can access your content quickly, no matter where they are located.

Will it work with my caching plugin or my own CDN?

Usually yes. The plugin only looks for image URLs that point to your own /wp-content/ directory, so images already served by another CDN are left alone. It rewrites the exact address of the image without adding query parameters, which keeps it compatible with most page rules.

What happens on a local or staging site?

The plugin stays inactive on local sites automatically, so your development images are never sent to wsrv.nl. See the list of local domains in the description above.

Does it handle SVG images?

No. wsrv.nl converts SVG files to PNG unless output=svg is requested, which would break vector logos and icons, so SVG files are skipped and served as usual from your own server.

How can I check that it is working?

There is no settings page. Open the source code of any page with images from your media library: the addresses will start with https://wsrv.nl/?url=.
sections.changelog:
1.2

  • Fixed the DNS prefetch: it now uses wp_resource_hints() (dns-prefetch and preconnect) instead of loading //wsrv.nl as a script, which generated a broken script tag.
  • Images are no longer wrapped twice when the page already contains a wsrv.nl address.
  • SVG files are skipped, because wsrv.nl converts them to PNG and vector logos lost quality.
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.1.
  • Readme improved: the description and the feature list now display correctly on the plugin page.

1.1

  • Fixed issue with static variable.
  • Updated WP version

1.0

  • Initial release.
